clue.text: Against Capone, say, law enforcement taking back all wine

parts.note: V is short for versus, meaning against
Al Capone, the gangster, is an example of someone called Al
the police are the body that enforces the law

indicators.note: taking back tells us the word all is read backwards

explanation.surface: A tale of the authorities going after Al Capone and seizing every bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ALL into LLA, which ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Valpolicella is a red wine from the Veneto region of northern Italy.

clue.text: Reduction in degeneracy, Conservative's success

indicators.note: a reduction means the word for degeneracy is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: vice is moral degeneracy
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A political claim that cutting moral decay is the Conservative party's achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduction in' docks the last letter of VICE, leaving VIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph or win is a success; the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Vaulted lodge lacking interior fitting

indicators.note: lacking interior means the word lodge loses everything between its first and last letters

parts.note: fitting means apt, suitable

explanation.surface: A description of a lodge with an arched roof but no interior fittings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking interior' strips ODG from LODGE, leaving LE. 'Vaulted' looks like an adjective for the lodge's ceiling but is the past tense of vault, to jump.
explanation.definitionFit: To vault is to jump over something, so vaulted is a past-tense synonym for jumped.

clue.text: With controlling position following cricket deliveries hit for six

indicators.note: following places the word for with and the controlling position after the cricket deliveries

parts.note: an over in cricket is a set of six deliveries by one bowler
the helm is where a ship is steered, the position of control

explanation.surface: A cricket report about a batsman, in command after some deliveries, hitting a six.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' sets the second part after the first. 'Hit for six' is British slang for being shocked, the cricket sense a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hit for six is a British idiom for being devastated or completely overcome.

clue.text: Oddly ignored big riot, centre of Santa Fe

indicators.note: with the odd letters of big riot ignored, only its even-placed letters remain
the centre of Santa is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A news snippet about a large riot being overlooked in downtown Santa Fe, New Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly ignored' keeps IRO from BIG RIOT; 'centre of' takes N from SANTA. Santa Fe reads as one place, but Fe is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fe is the chemical symbol for the metal, from the Latin ferrum.

clue.text: Cover the news travelling around area

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation for area
travelling suggests the letters of the news move about into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to a reporter to report the news while touring the region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges THE NEWS to ENSWTHE; 'around' puts that round A.
explanation.definitionFit: To enswathe is to wrap or swaddle something, which covers it.

clue.text: Welcome being ahead on racing circuit, say

definitions.meaning: to welcome something eagerly, such as praise, is to lap it up

definitions.text: being ahead on racing circuit, say
definitions.meaning: a driver a full circuit in front of another is a ...

explanation.surface: Greeting someone who is in the lead at a motor race.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap something up is to accept or enjoy it eagerly; a lap up is one circuit ahead in a race.

clue.text: Haggard oarsman going north in vessel

indicators.note: in means the reversed word sits inside the word for vessel

parts.note: a can is a vessel, a container

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means the word for oarsman is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a rower is an oarsman

explanation.surface: A worn-out oarsman heading north in his boat.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'going north' means reading upwards, so the oarsman runs backwards; 'in' places it within the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone haggard looks exhausted and drawn, showing the strain of worry.

clue.text: Defeated second-rate English/American team with a man down?

parts.note: B is a second-rate grade, as in B-movie
a football or cricket team has eleven players, so one short leaves ten

explanation.surface: A mediocre Anglo-American side, playing short-handed, loses.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beaten in a contest means losing it, so beaten and defeated are synonyms.

clue.text: Grass in neglected course is full of holes

indicators.note: in means the word for informer goes inside the jumbled letters
neglected suggests the word course has fallen into disorder, its letters jumbled

parts.note: to grass is British slang for informing on someone; a rat is an informer

explanation.surface: A golf course left to ruin, its grass pitted with holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neglected' jumbles the word course to CEROUS. 'Grass' looks like turf but is British slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Craterous means pitted with craters, so covered in holes.

clue.text: Fish leaving current location

indicators.note: leaving means the symbol for current departs from the fish's name

parts.note: plaice is a flatfish
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A fish swimming away from a current to a new spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes I from PLAICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A place is a location, a spot where something is.

clue.text: Old engineer set back advanced capital city

indicators.note: set back means the engineer's name is written backwards

parts.note: James Watt was the Scottish engineer of steam-engine fame
A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: An elderly engineer delays progress on a capital's development.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' turns WATT into TTAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital of Canada.

clue.text: Stewpan's converted as home for insects

indicators.note: converted means the letters of the word are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: An old cooking pot repurposed as a bug shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasps build papery nests that house their colony, so the nest is their home.

clue.text: Actor, Johnny, indeed making comeback, wittered on

indicators.note: making comeback means the words run backwards

parts.note: Johnny Depp is a Hollywood actor
ay is an old word for yes, as in indeed

explanation.surface: Johnny Depp returns to the screen and talks endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making comeback' reverses DEPPAY. 'Wittered on' is British for talking at tedious length.
explanation.definitionFit: To yap is to talk incessantly and pointlessly, as wittering on does.

clue.text: Petty Officer, clueless, heartless and pitiable

parts.note: PO is the naval abbreviation for petty officer

indicators.note: heartless means the middle two letters are removed from the word for clueless

parts.note: clueless means lacking knowledge

explanation.surface: A naval officer described as dim, cruel and pathetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops OR from the centre of IGNORANT, leaving IGNANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something poignant is moving and evokes sadness or pity.

clue.text: Switch off broadcast about Bletchley Park workplace beginning to drag

indicators.note: about means the word for broadcast goes round the other pieces

parts.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered, or sown
the wartime codebreakers at Bletchley Park in England worked in numbered huts

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of drag

explanation.surface: An instruction to turn off a radio programme about wartime codebreakers as it starts to drag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like radio but means scattered, as seed; 'about' wraps it round the hut and the D.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut down a machine is to switch it off completely.

clue.text: One that's flown over the Channel

definitions.text: One that's flown over the Channel

parts.words: One that's flown over the Channel
parts.note: seems to describe a plane or bird crossing to France, but means the French national flag, flown on the far side of the English Channel

explanation.surface: Something that crosses the English Channel by air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flown' suggests aviation, but a flag is flown; 'over' means on the other side of.
explanation.definitionFit: The French flag of blue, white and red stripes is known by this name.

clue.text: Popular when seen drunk, to some extent

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of seen stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is well liked, at least partly, when spotted inebriated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges SEEN as ENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something holds partly or in one respect is the meaning of this qualifying phrase.

clue.text: Arboreal rodent bit guards an hour after noon

indicators.note: guards means the word for bit surrounds the time

parts.note: a chunk is a bit or piece
one o'clock in the afternoon is 1 PM, with I as the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A tree-dwelling rodent snatches a morsel just after lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an' gives I, the Roman one, so an hour after noon is one PM; 'guards' sets that inside the bit.
explanation.definitionFit: This striped North American squirrel-like animal climbs trees and is a rodent.

clue.text: Upright army officer regularly selected gunmen

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer

indicators.note: regularly selected means every other letter of gunmen is taken

explanation.surface: A morally upright officer carefully chooses his armed men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly selected' takes UMN from GUNMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A column is a vertical pillar, standing upright.

clue.text: Wicked people taking king away from companions

indicators.note: taking the king away from means removing the letter for king from the word

parts.note: friends are companions
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Villains who abduct a monarch from his entourage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away from' removes R from FRIENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiends are cruel, evil beings or people.

clue.text: Gravel stored in smashing lean-to

indicators.note: stored in means the letters are kept within the words smashing lean-to

explanation.surface: Gravel kept in a splendid garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is a mass of small rounded pebbles, a coarse gravel found on beaches.

clue.text: Flag hung — sail at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of hung and sail are jumbled

explanation.surface: A ship with a flag and a sail hoisted out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner but is the verb to tire or weaken.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to lose energy and droop, which is to waste away or weaken.

clue.text: For all to see, nude rogue is improper

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal, suitable for every audience

indicators.note: rogue suggests the letters of nude go astray into a new order

explanation.surface: A naked rascal in plain view is behaving indecently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rogue' rearranges NUDE as NDUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Undue means excessive or unwarranted, so not proper or appropriate.

clue.text: Cut last pieces of fig roll, one creation of Mr Kipling

parts.note: to mow is to cut grass

indicators.note: last pieces of means the final letters of fig and roll

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Slicing the ends off a fig roll, a cake like those sold by the Mr Kipling brand.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Kipling is a British cake brand, which suits fig rolls; here he is Rudyard Kipling.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudyard Kipling wrote The Jungle Book, whose boy hero was raised by wolves.

clue.text: Shame being short of time, departs club

indicators.note: being short of means the word for shame lacks the letter for time

parts.note: guilt is a feeling of shame
D is short for departs, as on timetables

explanation.surface: Feeling ashamed at running late, a member leaves the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being short of' drops T from GUILT, leaving GUIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A guild is an association or society, which is a club.

clue.text: Flier written with some content you can ignore

indicators.note: some content you can ignore means part of the inside of written is dropped

explanation.surface: A leaflet written with filler text that readers can skip.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping ITT from WRITTEN leaves the answer. 'Flier' looks like a leaflet but is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A wren is a small songbird, which flies.

clue.text: Dug up object in auditorium

indicators.note: in auditorium means as heard by an audience

parts.note: to mind is to object, as in 'do you mind?'

explanation.surface: An artefact excavated inside a concert hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' looks like a noun for a thing but is the verb, to mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Mined means extracted from the ground, so dug up.

clue.text: Restricting liquor, ultimately managed to reverse being in debt

indicators.note: to reverse means the word for managed is read backwards

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of liquor

parts.note: owing means in debt

explanation.surface: Cutting back on drink and managing to get out of debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reverse' turns RAN into NAR, then the R from liquor, then OWING.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrowing something limits its width or scope, which restricts it.

clue.text: Driver's been uncertain about good way out of Wales

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation for good
uncertain suggests the letters of driver's been are unsettled into a new order

explanation.surface: A motorist unsure of a good route out of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The bridge over the Severn estuary carries the M4 motorway between Wales and England, a route out of Wales.
